summary: A one-time reduction of tuition fees offered by Trinity College Dublin to exceptional international students who hold an offer for a full-time postgraduate taught course. The student must be billed at the non-EU fee rate. The amount is between EUR 2,000 and EUR 5,000 depending on the student's region. Awards are chosen on academic achievement and the potential to contribute to the Trinity community. This page describes the 2026/27 round.
eligibility_notes:
You must have non-EU fee status, meaning Trinity bills your tuition at the non-EU rate.

You must hold an offer to start a full-time postgraduate degree at Trinity in academic year 2026/2027. The scholarship is for postgraduate taught courses.

Students from China are not eligible for this scholarship. Trinity directs them to its separate Claddagh Postgraduate Scholarship, which is for Chinese nationals living in China.

Business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are outside this scholarship. They have their own scholarship routes (business, and a joint route for engineering, natural sciences, computer science and statistics).

You must fully accept your course offer to receive the award.

The page sets no scholarship-specific grade, age, nationality list or language score. The course itself has entry rules: for postgraduate courses Trinity asks for at least a 2.1 honours degree or an equivalent result from another country, and some courses ask for more. English proof is needed from all applicants; the standard level for most courses is IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band, with other tests accepted (for example TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Duolingo, Cambridge). Results must be issued within two years before the course start, and some courses ask for a higher level.
funding_summary: The award is a single reduction of the tuition fee bill, worth between EUR 2,000 and EUR 5,000 depending on region. The page does not link specific amounts to specific regions. It is applied once to the tuition fee bill; the page does not describe any other benefit such as living costs, accommodation, flights or insurance.
programmes_note: Any full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity, except business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses. The page does not list individual programmes; students choose from Trinity's postgraduate courses.
institutions_note: Trinity College Dublin only. The scholarship is held at the course you hold an offer for.

requirements.text: Online scholarship form with your basic personal details. If you cannot open the form in your region, ask your Trinity Regional Manager or Advisor for an alternative form.
A short statement on how you will contribute to the Trinity community, entered in the scholarship form. No length is stated.

A course offer from Trinity for a full-time postgraduate taught programme for 2026/27. The course application itself needs: third-level results and transcripts for each year and all qualifications awarded, English language proof, two letters of recommendation, passport, and the non-refundable application fee (amount not stated). An application CV and personal statement are also part of that course form.

English proof for the course application: for example IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for most courses. Applicants whose first degree was taught wholly in English can ask the course director for an exemption with a letter from the awarding institution.
requirements.conditional_rule: required for the course application from applicants from predominantly non-English-speaking countries; some courses ask for a higher level

application_steps.title: Apply to your postgraduate course and get an offer
application_steps.detail: Apply through the page of the course you want. The online course form has nine sections, including English proficiency, education, personal statement, references and a CV upload; two letters of recommendation and a non-refundable fee are part of it. You need an offer for a full-time postgraduate taught course before the scholarship can be awarded; the scholarship deadlines below apply to the scholarship form. Each course sets its own course deadline.

application_steps.title: Check that you qualify
application_steps.detail: You must be billed non-EU fees and hold an offer for 2026/27. Students from China cannot use this scholarship and should look at the Claddagh Postgraduate Scholarship. Business, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are excluded and have separate routes.

application_steps.title: Submit the online scholarship form before your regional deadline
application_steps.detail: Give basic personal information and a statement on how you will contribute to the Trinity community. Deadlines for 2026/27: 1 April 2026 for Central, North and South America; 1 May 2026 for Africa; 15 June 2026 for all other regions; 15 July 2026 for South East Asia and Oceania. Applying early is advised because applications are assessed on a rolling basis. If you cannot access the form, contact your Trinity Regional Manager or Advisor.

application_steps.title: Assessment on a rolling basis
application_steps.detail: Trinity assesses applications as they arrive. Selection is based on academic achievement and the potential to contribute to the Trinity community. Allocations also take regional and programme diversity into account. The page does not name a selection panel or interview.

application_steps.title: Wait for contact after the closing date
application_steps.detail: Successful applicants are contacted after the closing date. If you hear nothing in that time, treat the application as unsuccessful: Trinity does not contact unsuccessful applicants one by one.

application_steps.title: Fully accept your course offer
application_steps.detail: You must fully accept your course offer to receive the award. The page gives no other conditions.

application_steps.title: Award is taken off your tuition fee bill
application_steps.detail: The scholarship is applied to your tuition fee bill as a single reduction. The page does not describe renewal or any reporting duty.
